title: SYSK Selects: Was Malthus right about carrying capacity?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on whether Thomas Malthus was right about carrying capacity. Hosts explain Malthus's exponential population vs. linear food growth argument, the debate with William Godwin, the demographic transition and replacement rate, Norman Borlaug and the Green Revolution, estimates of Earth's carrying capacity (two to forty billion depending on lifestyle), resource disparity, technology versus sustainability, greed, and the EV1 electric car. Closes with a listener mail about a mother sneakily getting her teenage son to listen to the show.

The Worst Mistake in the History of the Human Race

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Malthus and carrying capacity
segments.summary: Chuck previews the Selects episode, then Josh recounts first learning about carrying capacity in an anthropology class, using a population growth map and Jared Diamond's essay as illustrations. The hosts note world population near seven billion.

segments.title: Population growth statistics and Malthus's essay
segments.summary: The hosts cite population milestones and exponential growth, then introduce Thomas Malthus's essay arguing population grows exponentially while food grows linearly. They mention his debate with William Godwin, Godwin's perfectibility of society idea, and Malthus's views on eugenics and rent.

segments.title: Demographic transition and replacement rate
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how technology, birth control, falling mortality and education lower fertility, the replacement rate of about 2.1 children, low fertility in Western Europe and Asia, and high fertility in Africa, arguing Malthus did not account for these.

segments.title: Agriculture and the Green Revolution
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the shift from hunter-gatherer life to agriculture raised the carrying capacity, and how Norman Borlaug's Green Revolution techniques of high-yield crops, pesticides and fertilizer averted predicted mass starvation.

segments.title: Estimates of carrying capacity and lifestyle
segments.summary: The hosts explain estimates of Earth's carrying capacity ranging from two billion to forty billion, depending on lifestyle. They contrast middle-class American consumption with subsistence needs, and note the minimum requirements scenario and the diet implications of meat consumption.

segments.title: Technology, sustainability, greed and the EV1
segments.summary: The hosts argue technology is used to get more from more rather than more from less, discuss the optimist versus gloom-and-doom camps, and say greed is the flaw in the optimist model. They mention the EV1 electric car being recalled and crushed, and debate whether responsibility lies with individuals or policy makers.

segments.title: Closing and further reading
segments.summary: Josh suggests searching for the topic on HowStuffWorks, and the hosts transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: sneaky mom gets teen son hooked
segments.summary: A listener from Portland, Oregon describes sneakily playing the show while her thirteen-year-old son Ethan, a fencer, cooked in the kitchen until he became a fan and now listens on his iPod. The hosts respond and ask listeners for review suggestions.
